test_title: PYST 14: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Identify the word in this sentence that contains an error.

He jumped in the pool with his clothes on.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is found in the word "**in**" (Option 4).
 
• In English grammar, there is a distinction between the prepositions "**in**" and "**into**" based on movement and position.
 
• The preposition "**in**" is used to indicate a stationary position or something already inside a location (e.g., "He is *in* the pool").
 
• The preposition "**into**" is used to indicate **movement**, direction, or entry from the outside to the inside.
 
• Since the verb "**jumped**" describes an action of moving from the deck to the water, the word "**into**" must be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He jumped **into** the pool with his clothes on."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "clothes"** – This is the correct plural noun form for garments.
 
• **Option 2: "pool"** – This is the correct noun used as the object of the preposition.
 
• **Option 3: "jumped"** – This is the correct simple past tense form of the verb.
 
• **Usage Tip:** Use "into" with verbs of motion such as *go, come, run, throw, dive,* and *jump* when the destination is an enclosed space or volume of water.
